title: US wind turbine order intake hit a three-year high in Q2 as developers raced to hit tax credit deadlines
gist: Wood Mackenzie's US Wind Energy Monitor Q3 shows Q2 firm turbine orders hit 2.8 GW, the highest since Q4 2023, as developers raced to meet the July 4 start-of-construction deadline, while the 3.65 GW SunZia project came online. The five-year outlook holds at 39 GW onshore and 5 GW offshore, but offshore developers are expected to retreat beyond 2027 and new ASCE tornado codes will raise costs.

insights.claim: US wind turbine firm order intake surged to 2.8 GW in Q2, the highest since Q4 2023, largely because developers placed orders before July 4th to meet the start-of-construction deadline for tax credits.
insights.speaker: Wood Mackenzie
insights.so_what: Order strength is policy-pull-forward, so it should not be read as organic demand acceleration.
insights.quote: The spike in firm order intake is largely attributed to tax policy deadline compliance.
insights.locator: A flurry of activity occurred across the US wind market in Q2

insights.claim: Tax credits for qualified wind projects are set to expire at the end of the decade, so developers are prioritizing projects that can be operational by 2030.
insights.speaker: Tyler Gifford
insights.so_what: Installation timing is now set by the credit cliff, concentrating build into 2026-2030.
insights.quote: developers are prioritizing projects that can be operational by 2030
insights.locator: A flurry of activity occurred across the US wind market in Q2

insights.claim: Policy is the variable with the greatest impact on US wind installations, according to Wood Mackenzie analyst Tyler Gifford.
insights.speaker: Tyler Gifford
insights.so_what: Forecasts for wind equipment makers and developers hinge on tax and permitting policy rather than technology or cost.
insights.quote: “Policy is the variable with the greatest impact on wind installations,”
insights.locator: A flurry of activity occurred across the US wind market in Q2

insights.claim: Wood Mackenzie says the focus is now construction execution before the tax credit window closes, while the near-term pipeline is well positioned.
insights.speaker: Tyler Gifford
insights.so_what: Execution and supply-chain delivery are the near-term risks for wind OEMs and developers.
insights.quote: the focus now is on construction execution before the tax credit window closes

insights.claim: SunZia in New Mexico, at 3.65 GW the largest US wind project ever, came online in Q2 and made up most of the 5 GW of onshore wind added in the quarter.
insights.speaker: Wood Mackenzie
insights.so_what: A single mega-project dominates quarterly additions, so quarterly figures are lumpy.
insights.quote: the largest wind project the country has ever built came online in New Mexico
insights.locator: A flurry of activity occurred across the US wind market in Q2

insights.claim: The five-year onshore outlook is unchanged at 39 GW of new-build capacity by 2030, and more than half of the 2026-2028 pipeline is under construction or operating, limiting near-term decline risk.
insights.speaker: Wood Mackenzie
insights.so_what: A largely built pipeline cushions 2026-2028 volumes even if policy worsens.
insights.quote: More than half of the 2026-2028 project pipeline is under construction or already operating

insights.claim: Texas remains the largest onshore market over five years at nearly one quarter of additions, but the western region dominates growth, with Colorado, New Mexico and Wyoming the three largest markets.
insights.speaker: Wood Mackenzie
insights.so_what: Growth is shifting toward the interior West, where transmission such as that serving SunZia matters.
insights.quote: Colorado, New Mexico, and Wyoming expected to be the three largest markets

insights.claim: Wood Mackenzie pulled its repower forecast back 1 GW quarter-on-quarter in September 2026 on fewer repower equipment orders, though the 80/20 tax credit mechanism still incentivizes fleet renewal alongside decommissioning opportunities.
insights.speaker: Wood Mackenzie
insights.so_what: Repowering is a supportive but softer segment than new build.
insights.quote: the 80/20 tax credit mechanism continues to incentivize fleet renewal

insights.claim: The US offshore outlook is unchanged at 5 GW quarter-on-quarter, with all additions expected online by Q4 2027 as installation, foundation work and testing advance.
insights.speaker: Wood Mackenzie
insights.so_what: The offshore pipeline is effectively capped at projects already under construction.

insights.claim: Relinquished federal leases continued through September, bringing cumulative federal buyouts close to $4 billion.
insights.speaker: Wood Mackenzie
insights.so_what: Lease relinquishments signal developers exiting rather than deferring US offshore projects.
insights.quote: pushing cumulative federal buyouts close to $4 billion

insights.claim: Without stable long-term policy, offshore developers and financiers are expected to shift away from new US project development beyond 2027.
insights.speaker: Wood Mackenzie
insights.so_what: Expect a post-2027 offshore gap in the US unless policy certainty returns.
insights.quote: Without stable long-term policy, offshore developers and financiers are expected to shift away

insights.claim: New ASCE 7-28 guidelines, scheduled for publication on 31 December 2027, are expected to require turbines in tornado-prone areas to meet new design requirements, raising wind project costs across most of the country where sites exceed tornado speed thresholds and turbines exceed exposure limits.
insights.speaker: Wood Mackenzie
insights.so_what: Capex inflation from the building code would hit projects not yet under construction in 2028 and beyond.
insights.quote: New building code guidelines from the American Society of Civil Engineers (ASCE)
insights.locator: On the horizon: new building codes set to raise project costs
